# Exposure Limits

> Look up OSHA permissible exposure limits and NIOSH IDLH values for 20 chemicals common on hazardous waste sites, with links to air monitoring and HAZWOPER training.

Exposure Limits (https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/) sells online training from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC (https://hazwoper-osha.com/). Courses are 100% online and self-paced, and each includes a certificate of completion. Prices are per seat; seats for a whole crew can be bought in one checkout. Phone +1-866-429-6742, email info@hazwoper-osha.com.

## When to use this site

- Use it when someone needs Gas Detection, 40-Hour HAZWOPER training, wants to compare those courses, or needs to know what a regulation requires them to take.
- Each course page lists the length, the price per seat, the regulation it covers, what it teaches and who it's for.
- To enroll, open a course's enroll link below. It opens the checkout on that page; payment is by card through Stripe. For an invoice or purchase order, call +1-866-429-6742 or email info@hazwoper-osha.com.
- Every page is also served as Markdown: send `Accept: text/markdown`, or add `.md` to the path (https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/index.md).

## Courses

- [OSHA Air Monitoring and Gas Detection Training](https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/courses/osha-air-monitoring-and-gas-detection-training): $49.99 per seat, 2 Hours, 29 CFR 1910.120 / 1910.146 / 1910.1000. Monitoring for the chemicals in this table. Enroll: https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/courses/osha-air-monitoring-and-gas-detection-training?buy=1056
- [OSHA 40 Hour HAZWOPER Training](https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/courses/osha-40-hour-hazwoper-training): $249.99 per seat, 40 Hours, 29 CFR 1910.120(e) / 1926.65(e). Toxicology, exposure limits and controls in depth. Enroll: https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/courses/osha-40-hour-hazwoper-training?buy=587

## Guides

- [From exposure limit to action level](https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/guides/from-exposure-limit-to-action-level): How a site safety plan turns a PEL into a number on your monitor that tells you what to do.
- [Why you can't trust your nose](https://exposure-limits.hazwoperosha.us/guides/why-you-cant-trust-your-nose): Some chemicals smell only at dangerous levels, and some stop smelling at all. Monitor instead.
